_about: Published, group-level picture-naming results for people with aphasia and controls without brain injury, used as reference profiles in the Model Lab. Only numbers printed in the cited sources; no individual-level data. Category names follow metalesionlab.naming_errors: Nonword = phonologically related nonword, Neologism = abstruse (unrelated) nonword. Checked against the sources on 2026-10-26.

schwartz2012.citation: Schwartz MF, Faseyitan O, Kim J, Coslett HB (2012). The dorsal stream contribution to phonological retrieval in object naming. Brain 135(12):3799-3814.
schwartz2012.note: Philadelphia Naming Test (PNT), 175 items; Western Aphasia Battery (WAB) subtypes. With severity as a covariate, the authors found no group effects on these measures, so compare at matched accuracy.

walker2018.citation: Walker GM, Hickok G, Fridriksson J (2018). A cognitive psychometric model for assessment of picture naming abilities in aphasia. Psychological Assessment 30(6):809-826.
walker2018.note: 365 people with aphasia x 175 PNT items = 63,875 trials, all subtypes pooled. Non-naming attempts include omissions, descriptions, non-nouns, picture parts and fragments.

dell2007.citation: Dell GS, Martin N, Schwartz MF (2007). A case-series test of the interactive two-step model of lexical access: predicting word repetition from picture naming. Journal of Memory and Language 56(4):490-520.
dell2007.note: 65 people with aphasia. Responses outside these six categories were removed and proportions rescaled to sum to 1; nonword combines related and abstruse nonwords.

roach1996.citation: Roach A, Schwartz MF, Martin N, Grewal RS, Brecher A (1996). The Philadelphia Naming Test: scoring and rationale. Clinical Aphasiology 24:121-133.

walker2011.citation: Walker GM, Schwartz MF, Kimberg DY, Faseyitan O, Brecher A, Dell GS, Coslett HB (2011). Support for anterior temporal involvement in semantic error production in aphasia: new evidence from VLSM. Brain and Language 117(3):110-122.
walker2011.note: 20 participants without brain injury (unpublished norms reported in the paper).

yang2026.citation: Yang Y, Guan X, Arheix-Parras S, Ahmadi S, Newman-Norlund R, Bonilha L, Rorden C, Fridriksson J, Desai RH, Nelakuditi S (2026). Lesioned multimodal language models reproduce aphasic picture-naming patterns. arXiv:2607.11621v2 (preprint).
yang2026.note: 278 people with aphasia from the C-STAR cohort (University of South Carolina); group means of PNT response counts out of 175. Neologism covers all non-lexical forms; No Response includes descriptions. Shown with the authors' permission; group averages only.

mrri_guide.citation: Moss Rehabilitation Research Institute. Detailed Guide to Philadelphia Naming Test (PNT) Scoring (1996).
mrri_guide.note: Source of the sound-relatedness criterion used by naming_errors (shared stressed vowel, initial or final phoneme, or two or more phonemes).

subtype_profiles.measures: mean proportion of the 175 PNT responses; nonword = all nonword errors (related + abstruse)

pooled_profiles.name: People with aphasia, C-STAR cohort (N = 278)
pooled_profiles.mapping: AnyNonword = our Nonword + Neologism; NoResponse = our NoResponse + Description.

pooled_profiles.name: People with aphasia, all subtypes (N = 65)
pooled_profiles.mapping: Drop our Description and NoResponse, merge Nonword + Neologism into AnyNonword, then rescale to 1.
